memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak, and I don't think it clears the bar.

The strongest points are that the coin is alive, the class is ORGANIC rather than factory, there was no airdrop dump, and the top-3 holder share is low at 7.6%. In the first two minutes after graduation, about 307 buyers spent 163 SOL, and the top-5 buyer share was only 20%. That is some sign of broad early interest.

But the last 15 minutes point the other way. Net flow is -29 SOL, with sellers (251) far outnumbering buyers (159), and the price is down 70% in that window and 81% over 30 minutes. The drawdown from the 30-minute high is 87%. Sell volume exceeds buy volume, so demand is leaving, not building. Bundle share of 55% suggests much of the early buying was coordinated, and a launch bot was present. Buyers are also thin at this point and the pool is small (38 SOL), so a $20 ticket would face meaningful impact on both entry and exit.

No real case says demand is here and will persist for the next 30-60 minutes. The trend, the flow, and the drawdown all argue that the early buyers are exiting. I recommend skipping this coin.
memos.skeptic:
Most likely loss: a slow bleed plus fees, not a clean rug. The coin is already down 80.7% over 30 minutes and sits 86.8% below its high, while the last 15 minutes show sell SOL (108.83) outrunning buy SOL (79.76), net flow -29.07, and 251 sellers against 159 buyers. Early holders are exiting into a thin pool of only 37.76 SOL, so even a small bounce can be sold into, and at 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost plus impact, a dead-cat bounce barely clears breakeven.

The curve data points to insider distribution: 55% bundle share, a launch bot present, and a sell-to-buy ratio of about 1.02 right after graduation. The 35% completer share and a 198-second graduation delay add to that. The "ORGANIC" label doesn't offset this. Buying the dip here means catching a falling coin with a poor chance of recovery. Skip.
